shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.target: I can tell which attributes make a shape what it is (closed, number of sides and corners) and which do not (color, size, position).
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.ifCorrect: You can do this: can tell which attributes make a shape what it is (closed, number of sides and corners) and which do not (color, size, position).
shapes-equal-shares-skill-01.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking a turned square is not a square, or that color or size changes a shape's name. Try this: Turn and resize paper shapes; count sides and corners again.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.target: I can name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and rectangular prisms.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.ifCorrect: You can do this: can name circles, triangles, squares, rectangles, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, cones, cylinders, and rectangular prisms.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-02.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Calling every four-sided shape a square, or calling a cylinder a circle. Try this: Count sides and corners; for solids, look for flat faces and curved surfaces.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.target: I can put shapes together to make new shapes and tell how many shapes I used.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.ifCorrect: You can do this: can put shapes together to make new shapes and tell how many shapes I used.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-03.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking a new shape cannot be made from smaller pieces, or counting outlines instead of pieces. Try this: Use pattern blocks to cover a shape and count the pieces.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.target: I can split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal shares and name halves, fourths, and quarters.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.ifCorrect: You can do this: can split circles and rectangles into 2 or 4 equal shares and name halves, fourths, and quarters.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-04.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Calling unequal parts halves or fourths. Try this: Fold paper shapes so the parts match exactly.

shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.target: I can describe a whole as two halves or four fourths and explain that more equal shares are smaller shares.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.ifCorrect: You can do this: can describe a whole as two halves or four fourths and explain that more equal shares are smaller shares.
shapes-equal-shares-skill-05.ifMissed: Practice this skill again. Watch for this mistake: Thinking a fourth is bigger than a half because 4 is bigger than 2. Try this: Cut two same-size paper strips into halves and fourths and compare the pieces.
